build-busybox: Disable building the AR applet

When building with mingw32-make, it prefers executing commands
through "sh.exe" if it is available.

When busybox sh.exe executes "ar", it prefers executing its own
internal tool over a potential external tool found in $PATH.

(This can be avoided by setting 'export BB_OVERRIDE_APPLETS="ar"',
but as this build of busybox is expected to be used with llvm-mingw,
disable the built-in "ar" tool outright.)

build-busybox: Disable CONFIG_FEATURE_FAIL_IF_UTF8_MANIFEST_UNSUPPORTED

This allows running the built busybox on older versions of
Windows that don't support the utf8 manifest. (The utf8 manifest
is supported since Windows 10 update 1903.)

build-busybox: Disable make, copy mingw32-make.exe as make.exe

The built-in make is a POSIX make tool, which doesn't support
GNU make features.

As we do have GNU make, insert that as "make.exe" in the busybox
directory. Don't do that in the main llvm-mingw bin directory,
which can be used with other environments (e.g. msys2), where the
native make is to be preferred.

build-llvm: Bump to LLVM 22.1.0 RC 1

Some notable changes since LLVM 21.x related to mingw:

- Handle an uncommon error code in libcxx's std::filesystem,
  avoiding spurious test failures if running the libcxx test suite
  (noted at least occasionally on Github Actions)
- Reinstate x86 stack probe functions in compiler-rt, that we earlier
  beleived weren't used - but turned out to be used by GCC in i386
  mode
- Fix interpretation of a few corner case aarch64 SEH unwind opcodes
- Support for FAT LTO (compile with -ffat-lto-objects, link with
  -Wl,--fat-lto-objects)
- llvm-objcopy: Support the -p option for COFF targets
- llvm-readobj: A new option --coff-pseudoreloc for dumping information
  and symbols for mingw runtime pseudo relocations
- Lots of various fixes for the cygwin target
- Improve linking a custom CRT with binutils ld (by passing the custom
  CRT -l option at the same place as the original default -lmsvcrt)
- Make lld use the right mingw specific DLL entry point implicitly,
  improving some Rust use cases
- Fix running the libcxx tests with optimization for mingw targets,
  allowing more test coverage of the code generation paths

test: crt-test: Remove a comment which no longer is accurate

Since 9be66e9d22257ab008e1da58d2af3c3b9e0cacec, the F() macro
no longer uses strtod(), so the details about what strtod("NAN")
and strtod("-NAN") returns are no longer relevant.

test: crt-test: Prefer F(-NAN) instead of -F(NAN)

In the former form, the negation of NAN is hidden inside the
optimization blocking macro/wrapper. After
9be66e9d22257ab008e1da58d2af3c3b9e0cacec, F(-NAN) works just as
well as -F(NAN).

This avoids test issues with recent optimizations in LLVM.
https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/193586 seems to make
the compiler consider known symmetry for hyperbolic math functions,
exploiting the fact that cosh(-x) is equal to cosh(x) (for values
other than NANs). By hiding the negation inside the F() wrapper,
the compiler can't reason about is existence.

Revert "test: crt-test: Skip a test for cos(-NAN) == -NAN when optimizing"

This reverts commit 1d8c107d49ec09ff7a953e4cbcaa0c5137b9367d.

After 49e14021bee3a970cf29ed326c0b2fe0fc3dfb95, when using F(-NAN)
instead of -F(NAN) to hide the negation, this test passes correctly.
I hadn't realized that GCC and Clang optimized cos(-x) = cos(x), when
I made 1d8c107d49ec09ff7a953e4cbcaa0c5137b9367d (and at the time, the
F() macro didn't work properly with -NAN on all toolchains).

github: Don't add the bundled Python to PATH in test-llvm

Previously, we added the llvm-mingw bundled python to the head
of PATH, but we didn't expect to use it after all.

(In other tests, where we explicitly want to use the llvm-mingw
bundled python, we set -DPython3_EXECUTABLE="$Env:PYTHON_EXE.)

Previously (with runner image version 20260622.87.1), CMake ended
up choosing
C:/hostedtoolcache/windows/Python/3.13.14/x64/python3.exe, but
now (with runner image version 20260629.93.2) we ended up picking
C:/llvm-mingw/python/bin/python3.14.exe instead.

With the newer runner images, we do have
C:\hostedtoolcache\windows\Python\3.13.14\arm64\python3.exe in
PATH, but it is unclear why that doesn't get picked.

(Picking another version than the first one in PATH would make
sense if we'd have Python_FIND_STRATEGY=VERSION set. According to
the docs, that shouldn't be the default any longer though, and it
wouldn't explain why it picked 3.13 before when we provide
3.14.)

In any case, just skip adding our version to PATH since we
don't intend to use it, to make it use the system provided
version.

run-tests: Temporarily compile all executables before running them

When building throwcatch-main.exe, we link with "-L.". Since we
copy in the runtime libraries for executing tests, we might have
libc++.dll present if we aim for the target "test" while
compiling.

For arm64x builds, we could end up trying to link directly against
the arm64x libc++.dll rather than with the import library. Linking
directly against an arm64x DLL doesn't work yet in 23.1.0-rc1, so
avoid hitting this situation for now.

This is a temporary workaround; linking against an arm64x DLL should
work too, and the fix is being backported to the next RC.

Add ARM64X support

Extend the aarch64-w64-mingw32 prefix to provide ARM64EC libraries
alongside standard AArch64 libraries, replacing the separate
arm64ec-w64-mingw32 prefix. This aligns with how MSVC distributes
ARM64EC libraries and enables the linker to process both targets
simultaneously into a single hybrid binary.

This extensively utilizes LLVM's -marm64x option, compiling both
targets in a single compiler invocation to produce hybrid object
files (unlike MSVC tools, which require separate compilation passes).

test: Ignore failures to remove the output file in some cases

When running tests on Windows with busybox-w32 as shell, removing
the output log file for the stacksmash-asan testcase fails like this
occasionally:

    rm: can't remove 'log1-stacksmash-asan': Permission denied

This only seems to happen with the i686 build of busybox-w32, but
happens for the stacksmash-asan test built as either i686 or x86_64.

(If running run-test.sh repeatedly, it seems like the issue either
happens right away on the first iteration, or doesn't happen at all.)

Avoid breaking builds by simply making it ignore errors from this
particular "rm" command.

configurations, this is enabled by default.
